facts.content: Patient has a 1-day history of left-sided throbbing headache.
The headache began on waking yesterday, fluctuates, and never fully resolves.
facts.source_text: Onset on waking yesterday; fluctuates, never fully resolves

facts.content: Patient experiences photophobia, which improves when lying down and worsens in bright light.
facts.source_text: Photophobia; better lying down, worse bright light

facts.content: The headache is not related to coughing or bending.
Patient denies nausea, vomiting, visual changes, abnormal smells or tastes, fever, upper respiratory tract infection symptoms, and neurological deficits.
facts.source_text: Denies N/V, visual change, abnormal smells/tastes, fever, URTI sx, neuro deficits

facts.content: Paracetamol has been taken for the headache.
Possible trigger identified as work stress.
Patient has been on Microgynon oral contraceptive pills for 6 years.
Paracetamol is taken as needed.
Patient has nausea from acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin).
Patient's mother has hypertension and migraines.
Patient lives with friends, drinks alcohol on weekends, and does not use tobacco or drugs.
facts.source_text: SH: lives with friends; etOH few drinks weekends; no tobacco/drugs

facts.content: Assessment includes a new unilateral photophobic headache, possibly a migraine.
Consideration of oral contraceptive pill use.
Acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) intolerance is noted.
Start taking ibuprofen along with ongoing paracetamol use.
Encouraged to stay hydrated and rest in a dark room.
facts.source_text: Encourage hydration, rest in dark room

facts.content: Given red-flag advice: seek care immediately if fever, rash, worsening or persistent headache, or new neurological symptoms arise.
facts.source_text: Red-flag advice: fever, rash, worsening/persistent HA, neuro sx → seek care immediately

facts.content: Arrange blood pressure check and purchase a home thermometer.
facts.source_text: Arrange BP check; Purchase home thermometer

facts.content: If headache is recurrent, especially cyclical, or unresolving, start a headache diary and arrange re-review.
facts.source_text: If recurrent (esp. cyclical) or unresolving, initiate HA diary and re-review
